claims.statement: Docker Compose is the only supported way to run the application locally, and backend/frontend development commands must be executed inside their container via `docker compose exec <backend|frontend> <command>` because CI runs the same checks; Go microservice checks are the documented exception and run on the host Go toolchain (`gofmt`, `staticcheck`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`) or through `just lint-go`.

`docker-compose.yml` defines eight services (backend, worker, frontend, postgres, redis, mailcrab, indicator-service, mcp-gateway) with every published port interpolated from the root `.env` (BACKEND_PORT 8001, BACKEND_DEBUG_PORT 8090, WORKER_DEBUG_PORT 8091, FRONTEND_PORT 8002, POSTGRES_PORT 5432, MAILCRAB_PORT 8003, INDICATOR_SERVICE_PORT 8004, MCP_GATEWAY_PORT 8005); the two Go sidecars bind only to `127.0.0.1`, and the backend mounts the host Docker socket with a matching `group_add` Docker GID so testcontainers-backed tests can start a throwaway Postgres.

The tracked root `.env.example` is the single configuration source for the dev stack: `backend` and `worker` load it via `env_file`, Compose interpolates port/URL/`DOCKER_GID` variables from it, and the `frontend` service receives `VITE_*` plus `JWT_SECRET: "${SECRET_KEY:?SECRET_KEY must be set in the root .env}"`, so the SSR route guard verifies tokens with exactly the backend signing key and Compose fails fast when `SECRET_KEY` is missing.

For parallel work, `scripts/setup-agent-worktree.sh <worktree-path> <branch-name> [base-ref]` creates a git worktree (branching from `base-ref`, default `origin/main`, only when the branch does not exist) and writes a worktree root `.env` seeded from the main checkout's `.env`, falling back to `.env.example` and failing when neither exists; it then deletes and re-appends `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` (derived from the worktree directory name), `DOCKER_GID` and all eight discovered free ports, so re-runs leave no stale entries and concurrent agents get independent Compose projects without file or Docker conflicts.

`./scripts/agent-test` is the primary test entrypoint for agents (shorthand `just test …`), running on the host through `docker compose exec -T <service>` unless already inside a container or `--local` is given, sanitizing output and hard-capping it at `--max-chars` (default 3000).

The harness has three gates: Gate 0 runs lint/type checks (backend `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty check`; frontend `svelte-kit sync`, `svelte-check`, `eslint -f json`, `prettier --check .`) and halts without running any tests on failure; Gate 1 runs a path target with fail-fast; Gate 2 auto-detects ecosystems from the git diff and renders an Index plus Traces for the first 1–2 failures.

The harness exposes `--backend`, `--frontend`, `--all`, `--gate0-only`, `--no-gate0`, `--local`, `--json` and `--max-chars`, and the justfile wraps the common cases as `just test`, `just test-backend`, `just test-frontend`, `just test-indicator-service`, `just test-mcp-gateway`, `just test-scripts`, `just test-all`, `just lint-go`, `just check` and `just up` (which resolves DOCKER_GID via `scripts/docker-gid.sh`).

The agent harness covers only the backend and frontend ecosystems; the Go services under `services/indicator-service` and `services/mcp-gateway` are exercised by `just test-indicator-service` / `just test-mcp-gateway` (or `cd services/<service> && go test ./...`) and by their own CI jobs, and because `services/` is neither an ignored prefix nor a backend/frontend prefix, a Go-only diff detects no ecosystem and the harness falls back to running both backend and frontend.

Editing a backend model mandates generating an Alembic migration, and all migration files must follow the `<hash>_<description>.py` naming; manual SQL migrations should be created with the autogenerate command and use `op.execute()` inside the generated revision.

`migrations/env.py` imports every domain `model` module so all tables register on `BaseModel.metadata`, and overrides `sqlalchemy.url` from `DATABASE_URL`, rewriting `postgresql+asyncpg://` to synchronous `postgresql://` because Alembic runs a sync engine.

`src/commands/seed.py` always seeds reference data (`AccountTypeModel` and `InstitutionModel`), and only in the `dev` environment additionally seeds the test user, sample securities, accounts, positions, portfolios and integration users before committing.

`src/commands/flush_market_data.py` provides a mutually exclusive `--security-id <uuid>` or `--all` admin command that counts rows in `PriceModel` and `IntradayPriceModel`, requires an interactive `[y/N]` confirmation before deleting them, and invalidates the corresponding indicator cache (`invalidate_security` or `flush_all`).

`src/worker.py` builds a `MemoryHuey` instance in the `test` environment and a `RedisHuey` otherwise, imports `src.account.task`, `src.integration.task` and `src.market.task` at module level so their tasks are registered, and in its `on_startup` handler calls `huey_dashboard.init_worker_signals` and registers the worker's own `svcs` registry with a `NullPool` session manager (to avoid "operation in progress" errors across `asyncio.run()` cycles), while `on_shutdown` closes that registry.
Because the worker's `svcs` registry only exists inside a running Huey consumer, every task body guards on `huey.svcs_registry` and resolves its services through `Container(huey.svcs_registry)`.

The Huey dashboard is mounted by the FastAPI app at `/worker/api` by `src/main.py` calling `init_worker_dashboard`, which creates the huey-dashboard task table, registers Huey signal handlers with `bind_signals=True` and starts a Redis pub/sub listener; the task API is guarded by `current_user` and a WebSocket is exposed at `/worker/api/updates`.

The dev `worker` service runs the consumer under `watchfiles` with `--periodic` so edits restart it and the periodic scheduler is armed, and also sets `HUEY_DASHBOARD_WORKER: 1`, which nothing in this repository reads — the dashboard signal writes are bound by `huey_dashboard.init_worker_signals` inside `setup_worker_services`; the prod worker command is `huey_consumer src.worker.huey -w 2 --worker-type thread` with neither `watchfiles` nor `--periodic`.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on push to `main` and on pull request opened/synchronize/reopened with four independent jobs: `backend` (Python 3.14, `uv sync --dev`, `uv run ty check`, `uv run ruff check && uv run ruff format --check`, `uv run pytest`), `frontend` (Node 25, `npm install` in `frontend/`, `npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test:run`, `node --test scripts/opencode-go-session-fetch.test.mjs`, with job-level `VITE_*` and `JWT_SECRET` env), `indicator-service` and `mcp-gateway` (both Go 1.27.1 with `go mod download`, `go vet ./...`, an inline `gofmt` check, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`).

The `backend` CI job declares no Redis or PostgreSQL service because Redis is replaced by the autouse fake and PostgreSQL comes from the testcontainers fixture, so the suite must never depend on a real external service.

`docker-compose.prod.yml` keeps the same seven-service topology with built images, `restart: always`, explicit `container_name`s and fixed published ports (backend `8000:8000`, frontend `80:3000`); the two Go sidecars publish no host port and stay on the internal network, there is no mailcrab service and no `env_file`, and the worker runs `huey_consumer src.worker.huey -w 2 --worker-type thread`.

The root `Dockerfile` builds the backend image in two stages using `uv sync --frozen` (dependencies layer first, project second), copies the venv into a `python:3.14-slim` runtime as a non-root `appuser`, and runs `uvicorn src.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --workers 4 --timeout-graceful-shutdown 30` on port 8000.

The frontend production image is a two-stage `node:20-alpine` build (`npm ci` + `npm run build` with `VITE_API_BASE_URL`/`VITE_INTERNAL_API_URL` build args) that runs `node build` on port 3000, and both Go service images are static `CGO_ENABLED=0` binaries built from `./cmd/<svc>` into `alpine:3.21`, running as a non-root `appuser` with `wget` installed for their healthchecks on port 8080.

Migrations are not a deployment step: `lifespan_context` in `src/main.py` calls `run_migrations()` through `asyncio.to_thread` unless `settings.environment == 'test'`, and `run_migrations()` executes `alembic.command.upgrade(Config('alembic.ini'), 'head')`, so each backend instance upgrades the database to head as it starts.

Health probes are split by intent: `GET /health/live` returns `{'status': 'alive'}` without touching dependencies and is the check wired into the Compose healthchecks and Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK`, while `GET /health/ready` runs `select(1)` through the container-resolved `AsyncSession` and pings Redis, returning 200 with per-dependency `ok` values or 503 with `{'status': 'degraded', …}`.

Both dev and prod Compose files healthcheck the Go sidecars on `GET /health` (indicator-service with `wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/health`, the dev gateway with `wget -qO- http://localhost:$$PORT/health`); the indicator service adds `POST /compute` and the gateway serves MCP at `/mcp`, both unauthenticated on the internal network with graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM within a 10-second grace period.

This repository uses OpenSpec in `spec-driven` mode as declared by `openspec/config.yaml`; canonical specs live in `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md`, active changes in `openspec/changes/<name>/`, and archived changes in `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/`.

The four OpenSpec stages — propose, explore, apply and archive — are each defined once per agent tool, so they exist in four mirrored tool directories: `.agent/` (`workflows/opsx-*.md` plus `skills/openspec-*/`), `.opencode/` (`command/opsx-*.md` plus `skills/openspec-*/`), `.github/` (`prompts/opsx-*.prompt.md` plus `skills/openspec-*/`) and `.claude/` (`commands/opsx/{propose,explore,apply,archive}.md` plus `skills/openspec-*/`); `CLAUDE.md` exists as a single `@AGENTS.md` import, so Claude Code reads the same root guidance through the `.claude/` directory.

`/opsx:propose` creates a change with `openspec new change "<name>"`, then builds artifacts in dependency order using `openspec status --change <name> --json` and `openspec instructions <artifact-id> --change <name> --json`, reading completed dependency artifacts before writing each new one and never copying the agent-only `context` and `rules` blocks into the output files.

`/opsx:apply` reads the `contextFiles` returned by `openspec instructions apply`, implements each pending task with minimal focused changes, marks `- [ ]` → `- [x]` immediately, and pauses to ask for clarification (or suggests updating artifacts) when a task is unclear or reveals a design issue.

`/opsx:archive` never auto-selects a change (it lists them with `openspec list --json` and prompts when ambiguous), warns and requires confirmation for incomplete artifacts or unchecked tasks, compares delta specs at `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/` against `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` before offering a sync, and moves the directory to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>` (failing if that target already exists).
`/opsx:explore` is a thinking-only stance — reading, searching and creating OpenSpec artifacts are allowed, but implementing application code is not.

`.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml` is scheduled daily at 08:00 UTC and can be dispatched manually; it installs `openwiki` globally with npm, runs `node --test scripts/opencode-go-session-fetch.test.mjs` as a gate, then runs `openwiki code --update --print` with `OPENWIKI_PROVIDER=openai-compatible`, `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, `OPENWIKI_MODEL_ID=deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY` fed from the `OPENCODE_API_KEY` secret, plus a `NODE_OPTIONS` preload shim that adds the required `x-opencode-session` header and a non-generic user agent for opencode.ai requests and round-trips `reasoning_content` across turns for thinking-mode models, and finally opens a PR on branch `openwiki/update` restricted to `add-paths: openwiki` with `docs: update OpenWiki` as message and title.

The OpenWiki block at the end of `AGENTS.md` (delimited by `<!-- OPENWIKI:START -->` / `<!-- OPENWIKI:END -->`) declares a retrieval-first consumption policy for the generated `openwiki/` tree, describing it as an optional just-in-time evidence index rather than required startup reading: agents must not enumerate, preload or search wikis at task start, they use `openwiki_search` for just-in-time context and `openwiki_read` for the relevant complete sections when the user asks or when unfamiliar architecture or dependency behavior materially affects the task, a `workspace_required` response means asking which listed workspace to use and retrying with its ID, `openwiki_list_workspaces`/`openwiki_list_wikis` exist for discovering workspace membership, and when the retrieval tools are unavailable the fallback is reading the `openwiki/quickstart.md` entry point and following its links.

`just up` resolves the host Docker socket's group id with `scripts/docker-gid.sh` before starting Compose: the script `stat`s the socket on Linux, asks the daemon through a throwaway `alpine:3` container on Darwin (where the socket is remounted with different ownership), and prints nothing when no socket is mounted, in which case Compose falls back to `DOCKER_GID:-959`.

`tests/test_migrations_autogenerate.py` guards model/migration drift: it drops the schema and `alembic_version`, upgrades to head, runs `alembic revision --autogenerate`, and fails if the generated revision contains any `op.` call, deleting the generated file afterwards.

The admin CLI commands are run inside the backend container, and `seed_data` is idempotent-by-lookup — it selects before inserting rather than relying on constraint violations — so repeated runs do not duplicate rows; `tests/commands/test_seed.py` pins this by running the seed twice and re-asserting the same row counts.

The agent harness writes machine-readable reports to `.cache/agent-test/backend.xml` for the backend and `frontend/.cache/agent-test/frontend.json` for the frontend (deleting any stale report first so a missing report is meaningful), and exits 1 when anything failed, errored, or the runner itself failed.

Adding an OpenSpec stage means adding every tool mirror (`.agent/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode/`, `.github/`) because a change to only one silently diverges per tool; `.ai/skills/` is the canonical home of the wider non-OpenSpec skill catalogue (architecture-review, commit-message, feature-definition, orchestration, pr-review, quality-check, spec-writing, ticket-execution) that the three tool skill directories symlink, while the `openspec-*` skills stay per-tool copies — and `.opencode/opencode.json` sets the default agent `orchestrator` plus per-agent models (`orchestrator` and `pr-reviewer` on `opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash`, `implementer` on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `arch-reviewer` on `opencode-go/grok-4.7`, `spec-writer` on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro`).

The OpenWiki block in `AGENTS.md` keeps source code and tests authoritative (a brief's unknowns and review items are verification gaps rather than requirements), prefers the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior while preserving complete failure output, and instructs agents not to hand-edit generated OpenWiki pages but to update source code and docs and let the scheduled workflow regenerate the `openwiki/` tree.

`AGENTS.md` at the repository root is the entrypoint of the agent guidance hierarchy: it sets the communication style (sparse, filler-free, ask when unsure instead of inferring), branch and merge protection (agents never merge into `main`; ticket PRs merge into their `feat/<slug>` integration branch and only the user merges it), the agent workflow and artifact table, delegation of backend rules to `src/AGENTS.md`, frontend rules to `frontend/AGENTS.md` and Go service conventions to `services/README.md`, the Docker-only command rule for backend/frontend (Go via host toolchain or `just lint-go`), the harness and worktree instructions, and ends with the OpenWiki block; the area guides own their own workflow command lists, the no-external-services testing rule and the domain-driven / rune-class layering contracts.

The OpenSpec propose/apply/archive loop is a contract on a change directory: it is scaffolded by `openspec new change "<name>"` (never hand-written) and becomes apply-ready only when every artifact named in the schema's `apply.requires` has `status: "done"` — for `spec-driven` that is `proposal.md`, then `design.md` and delta specs, then `tasks.md` — and archive-ready when its tasks are checked and delta specs are reconciled against `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` before the move to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`.

The agent tooling is layered one owner per concern: `.ai/skills/` holds the canonical skills; `.agent/` holds `agents/`, the OpenSpec skills plus the wider catalogue and `workflows/opsx-*.md`; `.claude/` mirrors `agents/` and `skills/` and adds `commands/opsx/`; `.opencode/` adds `agents/orchestrator.md`, `command/opsx-*.md` and `skills/`; `.github/` holds `prompts/opsx-*.prompt.md`, the four `skills/openspec-*/` and `workflows/`; and `.ai/` is the durable output directory — `features/`, `reviews/` (`<date>-architecture[-focus].md`) and `notes/` (working notes and `<id>-plan.md`), plus the gitignored `scratch/`.

The orchestration skill defines a ticket pipeline over GitHub issues labeled `ticket` plus exactly one `status:*` (managed with the `gh` CLI, with new tickets created directly as `status:planned`, `status:pending` reserved for missing or invalidated plans, and transitions planned → in-progress → in-review → approved, a changes-requested loop, and a fallback to pending when the plan is wrong), assigns each worker a skill (`spec-writer`→`spec-writing`, `implementer`→`ticket-execution`, `pr-reviewer`→`pr-review`, `arch-reviewer`→`architecture-review`), and requires the orchestrator to merge approved, green ticket PRs into the `feat/<slug>` integration branch without asking while never merging into `main` — the final feature-branch PR is left for the user.

The harness's Gate 2 auto-detection ignore list is `openspec/`, `openwiki/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`, `.agent/`, `.claude/`, `.ai/`, `scripts/` and `frontend/node_modules/`, and `--gate0-only` combined with `--no-gate0` exits 0 immediately without running anything; when the rendered output exceeds `--max-chars`, at least half the budget is reserved for the Traces half so an oversized Index cannot starve the failure detail.

`openspec/config.yaml` contains only `schema: spec-driven` — the `context` and per-artifact `rules` blocks are commented-out examples, so this repository defines no extra project context or artifact rules for OpenSpec.

Two habits keep the change loop honest in practice: area-guide and skill instructions both route backend model edits through `docker compose exec backend uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "<msg>"` (the migration ships in the same change), and agents are told to write temporary artifacts to `.ai/scratch/` and working notes to `.ai/notes/` — never the repository root or `/tmp`.

`frontend/AGENTS.md` defines a four-layer frontend contract: `.svelte` files hold markup, styling and simple view state; `.svelte.ts` files hold rune-based ES6 classes for state and business logic (never destructured primitives, never module-level instances, `$effect` only for side effects); stateless `.ts` API clients own HTTP concerns; and chart drawing tools live in per-plugin directories under `frontend/src/lib/components/charts/plugins/<plugin-name>/` with a fixed module layout, strict no-cross-plugin imports, shared plumbing in `plugins/helpers/` and pure financial math in `$lib/utils/finance/`.

The dev `mcp-gateway` service builds `./services/mcp-gateway`, publishes `127.0.0.1:${MCP_GATEWAY_PORT:-8005}:8080`, receives `ENVIRONMENT`, `BACKEND_BASE_URL`, `MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN` and `DATA_PLANE_PATH` from the root `.env`, waits for the backend to be `service_healthy`, and healthchecks `wget -qO- http://localhost:$$PORT/health`.

In `docker-compose.prod.yml` the `mcp-gateway` service publishes no host port, pins `BACKEND_BASE_URL: "http://backend:8000"`, defaults `DATA_PLANE_PATH` and requires the shared secret through Compose's fail-fast `:?` guard (`MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN: "${MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN:?MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN must be set}"`), so the production stack refuses to start without it.

`just lint-go` is the Go gate for both modules: it fails listing the unformatted files when `gofmt -l services/indicator-service services/mcp-gateway` is non-empty, then runs `staticcheck@v0.8.1` and `govulncheck@v1.8.0` inside each service module; `just check` chains it after the harness's `--gate0-only` run, so one command covers Python/TypeScript lint and types plus the Go gate.

`just test-all` is a `[parallel]` aggregate over five recipes — `test-backend`, `test-frontend`, `test-indicator-service`, `test-mcp-gateway` and `test-scripts` — so it runs both harness ecosystems, both Go module suites and the OpenWiki shim's `node --test` suite in one command.

Both Go CI jobs pin Go 1.27.1 (for `staticcheck` compatibility) and run `go mod download`, `go vet ./...`, an inline `gofmt -l .` check, `staticcheck@v0.8.1`, `govulncheck@v1.8.0`, `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` in their own module, caching on that module's `go.sum`; the vulnerability scan is tolerated only when every reported issue comes from the Go standard library (the job greps for `standard library` and the absence of `from <n> module` rows), and any module-level vulnerability still fails the job.
The `frontend` CI job is also where the OpenWiki preload shim is tested: after `npm run check`, `npm run lint` and `npm run test:run` it runs `node --test scripts/opencode-go-session-fetch.test.mjs`.

The root `.env` carries the gateway wiring (`MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN`, `DATA_PLANE_PATH`, `MCP_GATEWAY_URL` and `BACKEND_BASE_URL`), and `README.md` tells existing checkouts to add `MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN` (the dev default `dev-market-data-token` or a real secret) because without it the backend data plane returns `401` to the MCP gateway.

`AGENTS.md` defines the pipeline artifacts and their homes: feature specs in `.ai/features/<slug>.md` with `status: draft → ready → done`, architecture reviews in `.ai/reviews/<YYYY-MM-DD>-architecture[-<focus>].md` with `status: open → resolved`, tickets as GitHub issues labeled `ticket` plus `status:*`, PR verdicts appended to the ticket's `## Review feedback`, optional working notes in `.ai/notes/<id>-plan.md`, and gitignored scratch in `.ai/scratch/`.

`services/README.md` fixes the shared Go conventions: each service is an independent module with `cmd/<service>/main.go` wiring plus `internal/{config,logging,httpapi,<domain>}/`; configuration is parsed by an injected `Load(getenv)` that fails fast naming the offending variable; logging uses `log/slog` (JSON at INFO in prod, text at DEBUG otherwise, `LOG_LEVEL` override) with access logs graded by response status; every request carries an `X-Request-ID` (propagated or generated, echoed and stored in the request context); servers shut down gracefully on SIGINT/SIGTERM within a bounded ~10s grace period; and Dockerfiles are multi-stage `golang:<v>-alpine` → `alpine:<v>` builds of `./cmd/<svc>` with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, running as `appuser` and exposing `GET /health`. A shared Go module was evaluated and rejected, so conventions are shared through documentation rather than code.

`python -m src.commands.export_data_plane_contract` regenerates the data-plane OpenAPI snapshot at `tests/market/contracts/data_plane_openapi.json` by slicing the FastAPI app's `/api/v1/market/data` routes, which is the contract the Go gateway's tests consume.

The dev `backend` service runs as uid/gid `1000:1000` with `UV_CACHE_DIR` and `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` under `/app/.cache`, starts with `uv sync && uv run uvicorn src.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --timeout-graceful-shutdown 30`, healthchecks `/health/live`, and depends on `postgres`, `redis` and `mailcrab`.
